widgets_values:
## Portraius Studio on your GPU: draft shots with AI

The Director's "Draft with AI" on your GPU: Gemma 4 plans the shot list for the Tour's sample scene, with the app's system prompt and scene card, and the shot schema written into the prompt. The plan comes back as text in **Preview as Text**; the app checks each shot and adds it to the scene.

Free: open-weight models and ComfyUI's own nodes, so no account or credits. Built by the app's own local adapters from the request its studio makes, so it matches what "On your GPU" sends (docs/local-setup.md).

**Models (Gemma 4 12B).** Every file is Apache 2.0.

| Folder in `ComfyUI/models/` | File | GB |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text_encoders` | [gemma4_12b_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/gemma-4/resolve/main/text_encoders/gemma4_12b_int8_convrot.safetensors) | 12.1 |

nodes.title: Generate Text
widgets_values:
Title: The Letter, again
Logline: A retired harbour pilot finds a letter he never sent.
Location: A late-night diner with red vinyl booths
Frame: 16:9
Film: Genre Drama, Camera Digital cinema, Era Present day, Pacing Standard
Cast (write each as its {slot} in the action):
- {lead}: Walt Harmon, a person. Retired harbour pilot. Tall and lean, usually in a navy wool peacoat over a dark knit sweater.

Answer with JSON only, no other text: {"shots":[{"action":"...","size":"...","angle":"...","lens":"...","aperture":"","movement":"...","lighting":"","durationSec":5,"continuity":"cut"}]}
size is one of: ECU, CU, MCU, MS, WS, EWS.
angle is one of: eye, low, high, overhead, dutch.
lens is one of: 24mm, 35mm, 50mm, 85mm, 135mm, anamorphic.
aperture is empty or one of: f1.4, f2, f2.8, f4, f5.6, f8, f11.
movement is one of: static, slow-push-in, pull-back, dolly-left, dolly-right, orbit, crane-up, handheld-follow, whip-pan.
lighting is empty or one of: soft-key, noon-sun, golden-hour, neon, practicals, moonlight.
durationSec is one of: 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15.

You plan shot lists for short film scenes in Portraius Studio's Director.
Each shot becomes one still and then a 4 to 15 second generated video clip, so describe one clear, visible moment per shot: what the camera sees and what moves. No dialogue, sound or inner thoughts.
Plan 3 to 6 shots that tell the logline with a beginning, middle and end, varying shot size and angle like an editor would.
Name cast members only by their {slot} exactly as given, never by name, and only cast members listed. Don't add other named people, brands, logos or real places.
Use the scene's location for every shot. Pick each camera field from the allowed values; leave aperture or lighting empty when the shot doesn't need one.
Set continuity to "continue" only when a shot picks up the exact moment the previous shot ends on, from a similar angle; otherwise "cut". The first shot is always "cut".
Match lengths to the pacing: calm scenes hold longer, fast ones cut quicker.
